standard_prerequisites.name: Surjection
standard_prerequisites.statement: A function f from X to A is surjective when every element of A is a value of f.
standard_prerequisites.use: Both directions of the proof exhibit a function and check it is surjective by unpacking this definition (929-931, 932-933).

standard_prerequisites.name: Positive integers and natural numbers
standard_prerequisites.statement: The positive integers start at 1 and the natural numbers start at 0; adding 1 maps the natural numbers into the positive integers and subtracting 1 maps the positive integers into the natural numbers.
standard_prerequisites.use: The shifts g(n) = f(n+1) and f(n) = g(n-1) move between the two domains (929, 932).

core_obligations: Forward direction: given a surjection f from the positive integers onto A, define g(n) = f(n+1) for n in the natural numbers; given a in A, surjectivity of f yields a positive integer n with f(n) = a, and n-1 is a natural number with g(n-1) = a, so g is surjective (928-931).
Backward direction: given a surjection g from the natural numbers onto A, define f(n) = g(n-1) for n a positive integer; every value g(k) is f(k+1), so f is surjective (932-933).
Conclude the two surjectivity statements are equivalent (884-889).

proof_roadmap.step: Shift the positive-integer surjection down by one and check surjectivity.
Shift the natural-number surjection up by one and check surjectivity.

difficulty_reason: The counted proposition is the author proposition at source lines 879-882: there is a surjection from the positive integers onto A iff there is a surjection from the natural numbers onto A. The author proof (884-889) must produce the shifted function in both directions, g(n) = f(n+1) and f(n) = g(n-1), and each direction needs a short surjectivity check against the definition of surjectivity, using that the domains differ by the single point 0. Both constructions and both verifications are required, so the unit is a real if small argument about reindexing enumerations.
